subject: [RFC PATCH v2 00/18] mm: read the page cache without folio references

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about how to handle PG_rcu_free flag in the presence of multiple readers accessing the same file, explaining that it's set under a reference and cleared only by the free, allowing lockless lookups to read until rcu_read_unlock().
reviews.raw_body:
From: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

Reading a page cache folio without taking a reference would keep CPUs
that read the same file from bouncing its refcount.  But without a
reference the folio can be freed, and its memory reused, while the
reader copies from it.

Add PG_rcu_free: the free of a folio with the flag waits for an RCU
grace period.  A reader that saw the flag under rcu_read_lock(), and
then still found the folio where it looked, can read it until
rcu_read_unlock().  A split copies the flag, as such a reader may still
be reading the new folios.

The folios wait on per-CPU lists, one grace period in flight per CPU:
call_rcu() per folio would queue a callback for every folio of a
truncated file.  A work, which can reschedule, frees each batch.
Reclaim depends on these frees, so the workqueue is WQ_MEM_RECLAIM.

The flag is 64-bit only (CONFIG_PAGE_RCU_FREE): page flags are scarce
on 32-bit, and the contention this avoids is a problem of large
machines.  It is off on PREEMPT_RT, where expedited grace periods are
normal ones, so the waiting pages cannot be freed quickly when memory
runs short.

pgfree_rcu in /proc/vmstat counts the deferred pages.  Nothing sets the
flag yet.

Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
[kas: rework for flagging at read time, 64-bit only and not PREEMPT_RT,
 shorter comments and changelog]
Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 include/linux/page-flags.h     |  21 +++++++
 include/linux/vm_event_item.h  |   1 +
 include/trace/events/mmflags.h |   7 +++
 mm/Kconfig                     |  15 +++++
 mm/huge_memory.c               |   1 +
 mm/memory-failure.c            |   4 ++
 mm/page_alloc.c                | 105 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 mm/vmstat.c                    |   1 +
 8 files changed, 155 insertions(+)

diff --git a/include/linux/page-flags.h b/include/linux/page-flags.h
index 7a863572adce..a1e52a1f8a52 100644
--- a/include/linux/page-flags.h
+++ b/include/linux/page-flags.h
@@ -111,6 +111,9 @@ enum pageflags {
 	PG_swapbacked,		/* Page is backed by RAM/swap */
 	PG_unevictable,		/* Page is "unevictable"  */
 	PG_dropbehind,		/* drop pages on IO completion */
+#ifdef CONFIG_PAGE_RCU_FREE
+	PG_rcu_free,		/* free only after an RCU grace period */
+#endif
 #ifdef CONFIG_MMU
 	PG_mlocked,		/* Page is vma mlocked */
 #endif
@@ -602,6 +605,24 @@ FOLIO_FLAG(dropbehind, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
 	FOLIO_TEST_CLEAR_FLAG(dropbehind, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
 	__FOLIO_SET_FLAG(dropbehind, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
 
+/*
+ * A lockless lookup that sees PG_rcu_free and then still finds the folio
+ * where it looked may read it until rcu_read_unlock().  Set under a
+ * reference, cleared only by the free.  Not for hugetlb or
+ * free_pages_nolock().
+ */
+#ifdef CONFIG_PAGE_RCU_FREE
+FOLIO_TEST_FLAG(rcu_free, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
+	FOLIO_TEST_SET_FLAG(rcu_free, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
+	__FOLIO_CLEAR_FLAG(rcu_free, FOLIO_HEAD_PAGE)
+#define __PG_RCU_FREE (1UL << PG_rcu_free)
+#else
+FOLIO_TEST_FLAG_FALSE(rcu_free)
+	FOLIO_TEST_SET_FLAG_FALSE(rcu_free)
+	__FOLIO_CLEAR_FLAG_NOOP(rcu_free)
+#define __PG_RCU_FREE 0
+#endif
+
 #ifdef CONFIG_HIGHMEM
 /*
  * Must use a macro here due to header dependency issues. page_zone() is not
diff --git a/include/linux/vm_event_item.h b/include/linux/vm_event_item.h
index 2628ccda076a..cbe849701653 100644
--- a/include/linux/vm_event_item.h
+++ b/include/linux/vm_event_item.h
@@ -36,6 +36,7 @@ enum vm_event_item { PGPGIN, PGPGOUT, PSWPIN, PSWPOUT,
 		FOR_ALL_ZONES(ALLOCSTALL)
 		FOR_ALL_ZONES(PGSCAN_SKIP)
 		PGFREE, PGACTIVATE, PGDEACTIVATE, PGLAZYFREE,
+		PGFREE_RCU,
 		PGFAULT, PGMAJFAULT,
 		PGLAZYFREED,
 		PGREUSE,
diff --git a/include/trace/events/mmflags.h b/include/trace/events/mmflags.h
index 935893e5ea53..47c3411a75e8 100644
--- a/include/trace/events/mmflags.h
+++ b/include/trace/events/mmflags.h
@@ -117,6 +117,12 @@ TRACE_DEFINE_ENUM(___GFP_LAST_BIT);
 #define IF_HAVE_PG_IDLE(_name)
 #endif
 
+#ifdef CONFIG_PAGE_RCU_FREE
+#define IF_HAVE_PG_RCU_FREE(_name) ,{1UL << PG_##_name, __stringify(_name)}
+#else
+#define IF_HAVE_PG_RCU_FREE(_name)
+#endif
+
 #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_USES_PG_ARCH_2
 #define IF_HAVE_PG_ARCH_2(_name) ,{1UL << PG_##_name, __stringify(_name)}
 #else
@@ -152,6 +158,7 @@ TRACE_DEFINE_ENUM(___GFP_LAST_BIT);
 	DEF_PAGEFLAG_NAME(swapbacked),					\
 	DEF_PAGEFLAG_NAME(unevictable),					\
 	DEF_PAGEFLAG_NAME(dropbehind)					\
+IF_HAVE_PG_RCU_FREE(rcu_free)						\
 IF_HAVE_PG_MLOCK(mlocked)						\
 IF_HAVE_PG_HWPOISON(hwpoison)						\
 IF_HAVE_PG_IDLE(idle)							\
diff --git a/mm/Kconfig b/mm/Kconfig
index 604c58199acb..6e5341b0bf64 100644
--- a/mm/Kconfig
+++ b/mm/Kconfig
@@ -718,6 +718,21 @@ config PCP_BATCH_SCALE_MAX
 	  latency.  This option sets the upper limit of scale factor to limit
 	  the maximum latency.
 
+config PAGE_RCU_FREE
+	def_bool y
+	depends on 64BIT
+	depends on !PREEMPT_RT
+	help
+	  Reads from the page cache can copy from folios that are read
+	  again and again without taking a reference on them, so small
+	  reads of one file from many CPUs do not contend on the folio's
+	  reference count.  The cost is that memory freed from such
+	  folios becomes reusable only after an RCU grace period.
+
+	  64-bit only: it takes a page flag, and those are scarce on
+	  32-bit.  Not on PREEMPT_RT, where expedited grace periods are
+	  normal ones, so freeing the waiting pages on demand would stall.
+
 config PHYS_ADDR_T_64BIT
 	def_bool 64BIT
 
diff --git a/mm/huge_memory.c b/mm/huge_memory.c
index 1e5d68acf62a..25082949a4ca 100644
--- a/mm/huge_memory.c
+++ b/mm/huge_memory.c
@@ -3743,6 +3743,7 @@ static void __split_folio_to_order(struct folio *folio, int old_order,
 #endif
 				 (1L << PG_dirty) |
 				 (1L << PG_dropbehind) |
+				 __PG_RCU_FREE |
 				 LRU_GEN_MASK | LRU_REFS_MASK));
 
 		new_folio->mapping = folio->mapping;
diff --git a/mm/memory-failure.c b/mm/memory-failure.c
index a8b03e2920ba..7dde7c3c9a0c 100644
--- a/mm/memory-failure.c
+++ b/mm/memory-failure.c
@@ -211,6 +211,10 @@ static bool page_handle_poison(struct page *page, bool hugepage_or_freepage, boo
 			return false;
 	}
 
+	/* The free of a hwpoisoned page is not deferred: wait for readers */
+	if (release && folio_test_rcu_free(page_folio(page)))
+		synchronize_rcu();
+
 	SetPageHWPoison(page);
 	if (release)
 		put_page(page);
diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index 12fac9084c48..a371e92da273 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -1313,6 +1313,96 @@ static inline void pgalloc_tag_sub_pages(struct alloc_tag *tag, unsigned int nr)
 
 #endif /* CONFIG_MEM_ALLOC_PROFILING */
 
+/*
+ * Each CPU has at most one grace period in flight (@queued), covering
+ * @batch.  Folios freed meanwhile wait on @pending for the next one.
+ */
+struct rcu_free_pcpu {
+	spinlock_t lock;
+	bool queued;
+	struct list_head pending;
+	struct list_head batch;
+	struct rcu_work rwork;
+};
+
+static DEFINE_PER_CPU(struct rcu_free_pcpu, rcu_free_pcpu);
+
+static struct workqueue_struct *rcu_free_wq __ro_after_init;
+
+static void rcu_free_start(struct rcu_free_pcpu *r)
+{
+	lockdep_assert_held(&r->lock);
+
+	if (r->queued || list_empty(&r->pending))
+		return;
+
+	list_splice_init(&r->pending, &r->batch);
+	r->queued = true;
+	WARN_ON_ONCE(!queue_rcu_work(rcu_free_wq, &r->rwork));
+}
+
+static void rcu_free_pages(struct list_head *list)
+{
+	struct folio_batch fbatch;
+	struct folio *folio, *next;
+
+	folio_batch_init(&fbatch);
+	list_for_each_entry_safe(folio, next, list, lru) {
+		if (!folio_batch_add(&fbatch, folio)) {
+			free_unref_folios(&fbatch);
+			cond_resched_tasks_rcu_qs();
+		}
+	}
+	if (folio_batch_count(&fbatch))
+		free_unref_folios(&fbatch);
+}
+
+static void rcu_free_workfn(struct work_struct *work)
+{
+	struct rcu_free_pcpu *r = container_of(to_rcu_work(work),
+					       struct rcu_free_pcpu, rwork);
+	LIST_HEAD(done);
+
+	spin_lock_irq(&r->lock);
+	list_splice_init(&r->batch, &done);
+	r->queued = false;
+	rcu_free_start(r);
+	spin_unlock_irq(&r->lock);
+
+	rcu_free_pages(&done);
+}
+
+static void rcu_free_defer(struct folio *folio)
+{
+	struct rcu_free_pcpu *r = raw_cpu_ptr(&rcu_free_pcpu);
+	unsigned long flags;
+
+	spin_lock_irqsave(&r->lock, flags);
+	list_add_tail(&folio->lru, &r->pending);
+	rcu_free_start(r);
+	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&r->lock, flags);
+}
+
+static void __init rcu_free_init(void)
+{
+	int cpu;
+
+	if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PAGE_RCU_FREE))
+		return;
+
+	rcu_free_wq = alloc_workqueue("rcu_free",
+				      WQ_MEM_RECLAIM | WQ_PERCPU, 0);
+
+	for_each_possible_cpu(cpu) {
+		struct rcu_free_pcpu *r = per_cpu_ptr(&rcu_free_pcpu, cpu);
+
+		spin_lock_init(&r->lock);
+		INIT_LIST_HEAD(&r->pending);
+		INIT_LIST_HEAD(&r->batch);
+		INIT_RCU_WORK(&r->rwork, rcu_free_workfn);
+	}
+}
+
 static __always_inline bool __free_pages_prepare(struct page *page,
 		unsigned int order, fpi_t fpi_flags)
 {
@@ -1327,6 +1417,19 @@ static __always_inline bool __free_pages_prepare(struct page *page,
 
 	VM_BUG_ON_PAGE(PageTail(page), page);
 
+	/*
+	 * Not for a hwpoisoned order-0 page: it never reaches the allocator,
+	 * and page_handle_poison() takes a reference right after this free.
+	 */
+	if (unlikely(folio_test_rcu_free(folio)) &&
+	    !(PageHWPoison(page) && !order)) {
+		VM_WARN_ON_ONCE(fpi_flags & FPI_NOLOCK);
+		__folio_clear_rcu_free(folio);
+		count_vm_events(PGFREE_RCU, 1 << order);
+		rcu_free_defer(folio);
+		return false;
+	}
+
 	trace_mm_page_free(page, order);
 	kmsan_free_page(page, order);
 
@@ -6401,6 +6504,8 @@ void __init setup_per_cpu_pageset(void)
 	for_each_online_pgdat(pgdat)
 		pgdat->per_cpu_nodestats =
 			alloc_percpu(struct per_cpu_nodestat);
+
+	rcu_free_init();
 }
 
 __meminit void zone_pcp_init(struct zone *zone)
diff --git a/mm/vmstat.c b/mm/vmstat.c
index cb57714539fb..66ed017bde46 100644
--- a/mm/vmstat.c
+++ b/mm/vmstat.c
@@ -1343,6 +1343,7 @@ const char * const vmstat_text[] = {
 	[I(PGACTIVATE)]				= "pgactivate",
 	[I(PGDEACTIVATE)]			= "pgdeactivate",
 	[I(PGLAZYFREE)]				= "pglazyfree",
+	[I(PGFREE_RCU)]				= "pgfree_rcu",
 
 	[I(PGFAULT)]				= "pgfault",
 	[I(PGMAJFAULT)]				= "pgmajfault",
--

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the reuse of page cache folios in fuse and virtio consoles, specifically that stolen pipe buffers are reused without being freed. The author agrees to remove the ->try_steal function from page_cache_pipe_buf_ops, which will prevent this issue.
reviews.raw_body:
From: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

PG_rcu_free holds back the reuse of a folio's memory until a grace
period after the folio is freed.  A stolen page cache pipe buffer is
reused without being freed: remove_mapping() takes the folio out of the
page cache and the caller keeps it.  fuse_try_move_folio() puts it into
a fuse file, where writes change it under a reader that found it before
the steal.

Drop ->try_steal from page_cache_pipe_buf_ops.  fuse_try_move_folio()
and virtio_console's pipe_to_sg() then copy, as they already do when
stealing fails.  SPLICE_F_MOVE from the page cache into a fuse file or
a virtio console now copies.

Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
[kas: rewrote the changelog]
Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 fs/splice.c | 51 ---------------------------------------------------
 1 file changed, 51 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/splice.c b/fs/splice.c
index 9d8f63e2fd1a..0133c2348da0 100644
--- a/fs/splice.c
+++ b/fs/splice.c
@@ -55,56 +55,6 @@ static noinline void pipe_clear_nowait(struct file *file)
 	} while (!try_cmpxchg(&file->f_mode, &fmode, fmode & ~FMODE_NOWAIT));
 }
 
-/*
- * Attempt to steal a page from a pipe buffer. This should perhaps go into
- * a vm helper function, it's already simplified quite a bit by the
- * addition of remove_mapping(). If success is returned, the caller may
- * attempt to reuse this page for another destination.
- */
-static bool page_cache_pipe_buf_try_steal(struct pipe_inode_info *pipe,
-		struct pipe_buffer *buf)
-{
-	struct folio *folio = page_folio(buf->page);
-	struct address_space *mapping;
-
-	folio_lock(folio);
-
-	mapping = folio_mapping(folio);
-	if (mapping) {
-		WARN_ON(!folio_test_uptodate(folio));
-
-		/*
-		 * At least for ext2 with nobh option, we need to wait on
-		 * writeback completing on this folio, since we'll remove it
-		 * from the pagecache.  Otherwise truncate wont wait on the
-		 * folio, allowing the disk blocks to be reused by someone else
-		 * before we actually wrote our data to them. fs corruption
-		 * ensues.
-		 */
-		folio_wait_writeback(folio);
-
-		if (!filemap_release_folio(folio, GFP_KERNEL))
-			goto out_unlock;
-
-		/*
-		 * If we succeeded in removing the mapping, set LRU flag
-		 * and return good.
-		 */
-		if (remove_mapping(mapping, folio)) {
-			buf->flags |= PIPE_BUF_FLAG_LRU;
-			return true;
-		}
-	}
-
-	/*
-	 * Raced with truncate or failed to remove folio from current
-	 * address space, unlock and return failure.
-	 */
-out_unlock:
-	folio_unlock(folio);
-	return false;
-}
-
 static void page_cache_pipe_buf_release(struct pipe_inode_info *pipe,
 					struct pipe_buffer *buf)
 {
@@ -155,7 +105,6 @@ static int page_cache_pipe_buf_confirm(struct pipe_inode_info *pipe,
 const struct pipe_buf_operations page_cache_pipe_buf_ops = {
 	.confirm	= page_cache_pipe_buf_confirm,
 	.release	= page_cache_pipe_buf_release,
-	.try_steal	= page_cache_pipe_buf_try_steal,
 	.get		= generic_pipe_buf_get,
 };
 
-- 
2.54.0

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed a concern that fuse_try_move_folio() should handle folios marked PG_rcu_free by copying them instead of refusing them, explaining that this is already the behavior for other cases where fuse cannot take a folio.
reviews.raw_body:
fuse_try_move_folio() takes the folio of a pipe buffer and puts it into
a fuse file, where writes change it.  A folio with PG_rcu_free may still
be copied by a lockless page cache read that found it before it left
the page cache.

Such a folio reaches fuse when a mapped file page is gifted with
vmsplice(SPLICE_F_GIFT) and its file is then truncated.
fuse_check_folio() refuses it only because the flag is not among those
it allows, and with a dump_page().

Copy such a folio instead, as fuse does whenever it cannot take one.

Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 fs/fuse/dev.c | 4 ++++
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+)

diff --git a/fs/fuse/dev.c b/fs/fuse/dev.c
index 4fec31fc0b84..526929c7b3f1 100644
--- a/fs/fuse/dev.c
+++ b/fs/fuse/dev.c
@@ -1152,6 +1152,10 @@ static int fuse_try_move_folio(struct fuse_copy_state *cs, struct folio **foliop
 
 	newfolio = page_folio(buf->page);
 
+	/* A lockless page cache read may still be copying from it */
+	if (folio_test_rcu_free(newfolio))
+		goto out_fallback_unlock;
+
 	folio_clear_uptodate(newfolio);
 	folio_clear_mappedtodisk(newfolio);
 
-- 
2.54.0

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the visibility of deferred folios in memory statistics, explaining that they have refcount 0 and are not on free lists, thus missing from all LRU counts and free counts. The author added counters for NR_FREE_RCU_PAGES to /proc/vmstat and show_free_areas() to account for these pages.
reviews.raw_body:
Deferred folios have refcount 0 and are not on the free lists, so no
counter shows them.  Memory that waits for a grace period is missing
from the free count and from every LRU count.

Count it per zone in NR_FREE_RCU_PAGES: nr_free_rcu in /proc/vmstat,
free_rcu in show_free_areas().  Preparation for freeing the waiting
pages sooner when they hold back memory that is needed.

Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 include/linux/mmzone.h | 1 +
 mm/page_alloc.c        | 4 ++++
 mm/show_mem.c          | 9 ++++++---
 mm/vmstat.c            | 2 ++
 4 files changed, 13 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/include/linux/mmzone.h b/include/linux/mmzone.h
index 94f9c3ff5416..3336b9e5ee99 100644
--- a/include/linux/mmzone.h
+++ b/include/linux/mmzone.h
@@ -228,6 +228,7 @@ enum zone_stat_item {
 	NR_ZSPAGES,		/* allocated in zsmalloc */
 #endif
 	NR_FREE_CMA_PAGES,
+	NR_FREE_RCU_PAGES,	/* freed, waiting for an RCU grace period */
 #ifdef CONFIG_UNACCEPTED_MEMORY
 	NR_UNACCEPTED,
 #endif
diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index a371e92da273..15bb66e36304 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -1348,6 +1348,8 @@ static void rcu_free_pages(struct list_head *list)
 
 	folio_batch_init(&fbatch);
 	list_for_each_entry_safe(folio, next, list, lru) {
+		mod_zone_page_state(folio_zone(folio), NR_FREE_RCU_PAGES,
+				    -folio_nr_pages(folio));
 		if (!folio_batch_add(&fbatch, folio)) {
 			free_unref_folios(&fbatch);
 			cond_resched_tasks_rcu_qs();
@@ -1375,9 +1377,11 @@ static void rcu_free_workfn(struct work_struct *work)
 static void rcu_free_defer(struct folio *folio)
 {
 	struct rcu_free_pcpu *r = raw_cpu_ptr(&rcu_free_pcpu);
+	struct zone *zone = folio_zone(folio);
 	unsigned long flags;
 
 	spin_lock_irqsave(&r->lock, flags);
+	__mod_zone_page_state(zone, NR_FREE_RCU_PAGES, folio_nr_pages(folio));
 	list_add_tail(&folio->lru, &r->pending);
 	rcu_free_start(r);
 	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&r->lock, flags);
diff --git a/mm/show_mem.c b/mm/show_mem.c
index b938cbcd774a..0d3bddbda108 100644
--- a/mm/show_mem.c
+++ b/mm/show_mem.c
@@ -204,7 +204,7 @@ static void show_free_areas(unsigned int filter, const nodemask_t *nodemask,
 		" mapped:%lu shmem:%lu pagetables:%lu\n"
 		" sec_pagetables:%lu bounce:%lu\n"
 		" kernel_misc_reclaimable:%lu\n"
-		" free:%lu free_pcp:%lu free_cma:%lu\n",
+		" free:%lu free_pcp:%lu free_cma:%lu free_rcu:%lu\n",
 		global_node_page_state(NR_ACTIVE_ANON),
 		global_node_page_state(NR_INACTIVE_ANON),
 		global_node_page_state(NR_ISOLATED_ANON),
@@ -224,7 +224,8 @@ static void show_free_areas(unsigned int filter, const nodemask_t *nodemask,
 		global_node_page_state(NR_KERNEL_MISC_RECLAIMABLE),
 		global_zone_page_state(NR_FREE_PAGES),
 		free_pcp,
-		global_zone_page_state(NR_FREE_CMA_PAGES));
+		global_zone_page_state(NR_FREE_CMA_PAGES),
+		global_zone_page_state(NR_FREE_RCU_PAGES));
 
 	for_each_online_pgdat(pgdat) {
 		if (show_mem_node_skip(filter, pgdat->node_id, nodemask))
@@ -325,6 +326,7 @@ static void show_free_areas(unsigned int filter, const nodemask_t *nodemask,
 			" free_pcp:%lukB"
 			" local_pcp:%lukB"
 			" free_cma:%lukB"
+			" free_rcu:%lukB"
 			"\n",
 			zone->name,
 			K(zone_page_state(zone, NR_FREE_PAGES)),
@@ -351,7 +353,8 @@ static void show_free_areas(unsigned int filter, const nodemask_t *nodemask,
 			0UL,
 			K(free_pcp),
 			K((unsigned long)this_cpu_read(zone->per_cpu_pageset->count)),
-			K(zone_page_state(zone, NR_FREE_CMA_PAGES)));
+			K(zone_page_state(zone, NR_FREE_CMA_PAGES)),
+			K(zone_page_state(zone, NR_FREE_RCU_PAGES)));
 		printk("lowmem_reserve[]:");
 		for (i = 0; i < MAX_NR_ZONES; i++)
 			printk(KERN_CONT " %ld", zone->lowmem_reserve[i]);
diff --git a/mm/vmstat.c b/mm/vmstat.c
index 66ed017bde46..64068d73d6d2 100644
--- a/mm/vmstat.c
+++ b/mm/vmstat.c
@@ -1212,6 +1212,7 @@ const char * const vmstat_text[] = {
 	[I(NR_ZSPAGES)]				= "nr_zspages",
 #endif
 	[I(NR_FREE_CMA_PAGES)]			= "nr_free_cma",

 #endif

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author acknowledged that a CPU freeing many flagged folios at once can hold a lot of memory, and agreed to restructure the code in v2 to take both lists when more than 4 MiB is pending on a CPU, and only expedite the grace period when the zone is below its high watermark or when the pages waiting in it are more than an eighth of its free pages. The author also explained that the expedited grace period interrupts every CPU.

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed the concern that reclaim fails to free waiting pages when they and other reclaimable pages would bring an eligible zone above its minimum watermark, agreeing to restructure in v2 to add a new function, rcu_free_drain(), which frees these pages straight to the buddy lists.

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the interaction between memory hotplug and RCU free pages, explaining that alloc_contig_range() and offline_pages() migrate folios out of a range but then check if every page is free, which fails when a migrated folio has PG_rcu_free. The author proposed to free waiting folios before checking, allowing alloc_contig_range() to find the start of the free range again.

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed the concern that compaction fails more often when migrating blocks containing PG_rcu_free folios, which are freed after a grace period. The author agreed to restructure the code in v2 to free pages waiting for a grace period before draining per-cpu lists and checking if compaction is done.
reviews.raw_body:
A block that compaction has migrated every folio out of becomes free
once those folios are back in the buddy lists.  A migrated folio that
had PG_rcu_free comes back only after a grace period, so compaction
finds the block still in use, migrates more blocks than it needs and
fails more often.  defrag_mode relies on compaction making whole free
blocks, and there it shows up as allocation stalls.

When compaction moves past a block it migrated from and the zone has
pages waiting, free them before it drains the per-cpu lists and checks
whether it is done.  The drain costs an expedited grace period, so
async compaction, which must not block, skips it.

Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
---
 mm/compaction.c | 8 ++++++++
 mm/page_alloc.c | 2 +-
 mm/page_alloc.h | 1 +
 3 files changed, 10 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/mm/compaction.c b/mm/compaction.c
index a049415512c6..2acb87a3446d 100644
--- a/mm/compaction.c
+++ b/mm/compaction.c
@@ -2760,6 +2760,14 @@ compact_zone(struct compact_control *cc, struct capture_control *capc)
 				block_start_pfn(cc->migrate_pfn, cc->order);
 
 			if (last_migrated_pfn < current_block_start) {
+				/*
+				 * Folios migrated away from lockless readers
+				 * are freed after a grace period.  Async
+				 * compaction does not wait for it.
+				 */
+				if (cc->mode != MIGRATE_ASYNC &&
+				    zone_rcu_free_waiting(cc->zone))
+					rcu_free_drain();
 				lru_add_drain_cpu_zone(cc->zone);
 				/* No more flushing until we migrate again */
 				last_migrated_pfn = 0;
diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.c b/mm/page_alloc.c
index eea287ab2a01..afd4343ad572 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.c
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.c
@@ -1457,7 +1457,7 @@ static void rcu_free_defer(struct folio *folio)
  * callers want to allocate the pages next.  A concurrent drain holds the
  * lock until it has freed what it took.
  */
-static void rcu_free_drain(void)
+void rcu_free_drain(void)
 {
 	static DEFINE_MUTEX(lock);
 	LIST_HEAD(list);
diff --git a/mm/page_alloc.h b/mm/page_alloc.h
index 764e3f43b3b9..4f5f06adbfdc 100644
--- a/mm/page_alloc.h
+++ b/mm/page_alloc.h
@@ -235,6 +235,7 @@ struct page *__alloc_frozen_pages_noprof(gfp_t gfp, unsigned int order, int nid,
 	alloc_hooks(__alloc_frozen_pages_noprof(__VA_ARGS__))
 void free_frozen_pages(struct page *page, unsigned int order);
 void free_unref_folios(struct folio_batch *fbatch);
+void rcu_free_drain(void);
 void rcu_free_sync(void);
 
 /* Whether @zone has pages waiting for a grace period */

reviews.author: David (Arm)

reviews.raw_body:
Removing code is always nice, even independent of the other changes :)

The description doesn't really describe the impact of this change. I assume a
slowdown of certain workloads (does anybody really care?), and temporary

2026-11-04.patch_summary: This patch series proposes a change to how Linux handles page cache reads, allowing multiple CPUs to read from the same folio without taking a reference. This is done by introducing a new flag PG_rcu_free and deferring the freeing of folios until an RCU grace period. The goal is to reduce contention between readers and improve performance in scenarios where many threads are reading the same pages. The patch series includes 18 patches that implement this change, including modifications to filemap_read(), shmem, and other related functions.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed a concern about SPLICE_F_MOVE not moving page cache folios between files since 2007, and asked for input from other reviewers (Miklos, Bernd, Amit) on whether the copy would hurt any users that depend on the move.
reviews.raw_body:
SPLICE_F_MOVE has not moved page cache folios between files since 2007.
See 485ddb4b9741 ("1/2 splice: dont steal").  The only users that still
steal from a pipe are fuse, when a server splices into /dev/fuse with
SPLICE_F_MOVE, and virtio_console's splice_write().  With this patch
both copy, and the source file keeps its folio cached.

Miklos, Bernd, Amit: do you know of users that depend on the move?  Would
the copy hurt them?

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David suggested refocusing the patch to only work with folios, specifically mentioning FOLIO_RCU_FREE

Reviewer David suggested splitting the folio RCU free infrastructure into two separate configuration options, one for enabling the feature and another for documenting its details.

Reviewer David suggested replacing the growing list of flags with a single const mask constructed using BIT() and __PG_RCU_FREE to improve code maintainability.

Reviewer David suggested intercepting on the folio freeing path instead of modifying the read path, proposing to place the handling in mm/folio.c and separating page vs. folio concerns.
reviews.raw_body:
I think we really want to focus this only on folios (like the current code does).

FOLIO_RCU_FREE ?

---

While that description is helpful, that's not really what this patch, or rather
the basic infrastructure in page_alloc, does.

I'd suggest to have a dedicated FOLIO_RCU_FREE config and maybe another one
(that selects/depends on) FOLIO_RCU_FREE that actually enables the pagecache use
and documents the details.

---

That looks a bit odd at first, as it's very different to the other once. But no
easy way around assuming that the flag is not always around.

Maybe we should just have this be a const mask constructed somewhere using BIT()
and __PG_RCU_FREE etc, instead of having this growing list in this user here.

---

I'm wondering whether we want to intercept on the folio freeing path instead?
That would be __folio_put(), before we go into free_frozen_pages() used by other
machinery that does not apply (slab etc).

So maybe this handling could be placed into mm/folio.c instead, just a quick
thought ... reading about folio batches above I think that might be the right
direction, we are mixing too much page vs. folio things here.

-- 
Cheers,

David
